speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in today. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; to help me understand what is happening, can you tell me how long these episodes typically last and whether you lose consciousness completely?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Frontal Lobe Epilepsy (specifically suggesting an Epilepsia Partialis Continua or focal aware/impairing seizure with secondary generalization).

The "muddy taste" (gustatory aura) and hand gestures are highly suggestive of focal onset seizures originating in the insula or frontal lobe. Given the age and semiology, could you tell me if there is any family history of seizures or if these events have ever occurred while he was sleeping?
